ety.text: From веретено́ (veretenó) + -о- (-o-) + о́браз (óbraz) + -ный (-nyj), a calque of New Latin fusiformis.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *věrьnostь. By surface analysis, ве́рный (vérnyj) + -ость (-ostʹ).

ety.text: By surface analysis, но́вый (nóvyj, “new”) + Двина́ (Dviná, ellipsis of Се́верная Двина́ (Sévernaja Dviná, “Northern Dvina”), the river it is situated next to) + -ск (-sk, placename suffix). Coined in 1977, when the town was granted town status. The town was originally named Вороши́ловский (Vorošílovskij), and was later changed to Первома́йский (Pervomájskij) in the late 1950s.

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic озарити (ozariti), from Proto-Slavic *ozariti. By surface analysis, о- (o-) + заря́ (zarjá) + -и́ть (-ítʹ).

ety.text: Lexicalization of пожа́луй (požáluj) + -ста (-sta), an obsolete clitic that was used to add emphasis and to signify politeness, of obscure origin. The clitic is no longer used or known to most speakers, even as passive vocabulary, and has essentially disappeared from the language. Accordingly, to modern speakers, the ending of the word пожалуйста is merely a sequence of sounds of indeterminate meaning. The letter й, despite still being used in the spelling, was dropped from the pronunciation.

s.g: native or inhabitant of Poznań (usually male)

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic рубежь (rubežĭ), from Proto-Slavic *rǫbežь, from *rǫbiti (“to chop, hem”) + *-ežь. Doublet of рубёж (rubjóž).
